chunks: And do not invoke besides Allah that which can neither benefit you nor harm you; for if you do, then indeed you will be of the unjust.
ai.seo_question: Why is invoking other than God considered injustice in Islam?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah Yunus is often cited to distinguish between minor polytheism (shirk asghar) in supplication and major polytheism in lordship, emphasizing that calling upon idols or saints who cannot independently benefit or harm constitutes self-injustice. The term 'al-zalimin' (the unjust) is interpreted as referring primarily to the self, highlighting the internal spiritual cost of misdirected devotion. This reinforces the concept of tawhid in action, where exclusive reliance on God preserves the integrity of one's worship.
